messages:
acme-infra (customer): Hey team, our app started getting 502s when calling Redwood API through our interface endpoint. Direct calls from the same subnet to the public API succeed. Can we get a quick triage?
Jordan (support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you confirm you're hitting the interface endpoint DNS name (the one created by the VPC endpoint) and not the public hostname? Any recent Route53 changes?
acme-infra (customer): We're using api.acme-product.internal -> resolves to the same public CNAME as the internet hostname. We did a zone import last week but thought it was only internal zones.
Li (networking): Quick checks: run `dig +short api.acme-product.internal` from the app host and from another host in a different subnet, and `curl -v` to show the TLS handshake / SNI. Also check `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-***` to ensure PrivateDnsEnabled is true for that interface endpoint.
acme-infra (customer): Dig output from app host:```
$ dig +short api.acme-product.internal
52.24.11.9
```
acme-infra (customer): From a bastion in a different VPC peered via TGW:```
$ dig +short api.acme-product.internal
10.3.5.21
```
Maria (eng-infra): Uh — looks like split-horizon / PHZ behavior. From the app host it's resolving to the public IP (52.24.11.9) so traffic is leaving the VPC and hitting our internet path -> downstream LB that returns 502 for non-VPC-origin traffic. When it resolves to 10.3.5.21 it is correctly hitting the internal path.
Jordan (support): That explains the difference. Two likely causes: (1) Private DNS on the interface endpoint is OFF, or (2) there's a Route53 private hosted zone (PHZ) conflict/association missing for the app's VPC. Also check the VPC attribute `enableDnsHostnames` and `enableDnsSupport`.
Li (networking): Also confirm the interface endpoint's security group allows inbound from your app subnets and outbound ephemeral ports. If the ENI SG only allows 443 in but blocks ephemeral return ports, you can get TCP teardown/502s. NACLs on the subnet also need to allow ephemeral high ports (1024-65535).
acme-infra (customer): Running:```
$ aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0abcd1234 --query 'VpcEndpoints[0].PrivateDnsEnabled'
false
```
Maria (eng-infra): There it is. Private DNS is disabled. When PrivateDnsEnabled is false, the endpoint doesn't hijack the public hostname — your app's name still resolves to the public IP unless you have a PHZ that points to the private addresses and is associated with the app VPC.
Jordan (support): Two remediation paths: (A) enable Private DNS on the interface endpoint (if you're ok with it affecting that host/domain), or (B) fix the PHZ association so the VPC resolves the internal records to the endpoint IPs. If you enable Private DNS you won't need the PHZ mapping. Note enabling Private DNS modifies how the service name resolves inside your VPC.
acme-infra (customer): Is enabling Private DNS safe? Any gotchas?
Li (networking): Caveats: enabling PrivateDnsEnabled will create alias records in the VPC that point the service's public name to the interface endpoint private IPs. If you have a custom PHZ with overlapping names you might end up with split-horizon surprises. Also watch for cross-account endpoints and Route53 PHZ ownership. If you use DNS-based routing policies (weighted failover) those won't be visible inside the VPC — traffic goes to the endpoint.
Maria (eng-infra): Also verify your endpoint ENI SGs and subnet NACLs before flipping. If ephemeral/egress is blocked the request may start but fail midflow and surface as a 502. Check the ELB/NLB logs too: do you see connections coming from the ENI private IPs or public NAT IPs?
acme-infra (customer): We checked ALB logs: the source IPs for the failing requests are our NAT GW public IPs (so traffic is leaving), not endpoint ENI IPs.
Jordan (support): That matches — DNS resolved to public IP so traffic went out via NAT. For a quick fix: enable PrivateDnsEnabled on the VPCE, then from the app host `dig +short api.acme-product.internal` should return the endpoint private IPs. After change, clear local DNS caches and test.
acme-infra (customer): Doing the toggle now. Also updated the endpoint SG to allow 443 from the app subnet and allowed 1024-65535 in NACL. Will report back.
(deploy-bot): deployment vpce-config-update-2023-08-11 succeeded in 2m 4s — changed vpce PrivateDnsEnabled: true, modified gp2:NACL and sg:vpce-endpoint rules.
acme-infra (customer): Post-change dig:```
$ dig +short api.acme-product.internal
10.10.4.23
```
acme-infra (customer): Curl now returns 200 from the app host. Thanks!
Li (networking): OK great. Follow-ups: - if you run multi-region, consider endpoint failover / control plane routing. - Document the PHZ ownership model for any future zone imports so this doesn't re-occur.
Maria (eng-infra): I'll add a short KB note for support: checklist (PrivateDnsEnabled, PHZ associations, VPC DNS attrs, endpoint SGs, subnet NACLs, ALB healthcheck source IPs).
Jordan (support): Closing the thread once you confirm everything is stable for 24h. Glad it was a deterministic DNS + SG/NACL combo, not a runtime bug on our side :thumbsup:
acme-infra (customer): Will monitor. Appreciate the rapid help :heart:
